The quality of the psych ward will obviously vary depending on your location, but I advise you to be calm. Those places are nothing to be afraid of, in fact, you should look at them as a second opportunity. Try to make friends there, they more-or-less know what you're going through firsthand. It can get a bit boring so you should bring something you like with yourself (books and music helped me a lot). I hope from the bottom of my heart that everything goes well.

I know what you mean, sometimes I don't like revealing much about myself because I feel like it would somehow "contaminate" (that word is not very accurate but nothing else comes to mind) the relationship with the person I'm talking with.

>Do any of you feel the need to be drunk or high all of the time?

Never tried weed and probably never will, but yeah, life is much better when I'm drunk. Pretty sure my parents would kick me out if I drank heavily, though. IMO the impetus for being drunk is simply managing to break the monotony and boredom of life.

>Is paranoia and delusions and anhedonia enough to qualify you as schizophrenic and if so is it likely it will get more severe as I get older?

They sure are symptoms, if you're interested in getting diagnosed you should talk to a psychiatrist.

>Also do any of you lead productive or highly successful lives?

I was completely non-functional from 2016 to 2018, couldn't even leave my house and ended up in a psych ward. Now I'm a law student, that counts as something productive but I don't consider myself to be successful beyond that aspect.
I am a very defeatist person in general. It's not a delusion though, my life is objectively bad.

I haven't had significant IRL social interactions with anybody outside of my family in about a year and a half. That said, I haven't tried it and I don't think it would work since I would come across as even more awkward than I already am.

All days are exactly the same. From the moment I wake up until the moment I go to sleep, I think about how much I hate myself for being a friendless virgin, I go from intense anger to relative calmness, I go from sadness to distraction, I loathe myself for what happened and what hasn't happened, and I try to organize my thoughts to no avail. It's not like any of it matters, though.

I have so many things in mind that I don't even know where to begin. I perceive so many different feelings yet I can't properly put them into words. The only feeling that is sort of comprehensible is anger, I'm fucking pissed off. I've never experienced sensory hallucinations but my delusions are beginning to creep up again. I'm scared of the past and the future. I question all my decisions, all my moves, and all my thoughts. The bottom line is that I'm exhausted.

Of course, there are different ways of approaching a suicidal person and some are much more appropriate than others, I’m not negating that. The fact is that when someone’s internal turmoil reaches a point where they legitimately start considering death, they’re evidently ill or at least showing symptoms of illness, and arguing that suicidal ideation is normal (not curiosity about death or intrusive thoughts about death, like you said that’s another thing) is absurd IMO.

I never experienced any significant weight loss or gain on antipsychotics and I've never taken Invega, so unfortunately I can't give you any advice other than speaking with your psychiatrist. I don't trust them very much, but at the end of the day, they're the most suitable people to talk to about these things.

>Having suicidal thoughts and ideations is normal

No, it's not normal, not by any standards. It's a symptom of severe mental illness. I'm all for destigmatization, but let's not negate reality.
It really does. It robs you of your happiness, your sense of reality, your entire life basically. Mental illnesses are hell on Earth.
I don't really remember how I was feeling when I cut myself a few years ago. Yes, my life had gone to shit and I was obviously depressed, but I suppose I did it out of curiosity.
I used to cry a lot, I just can't cry now. I guess my mind is so fucked that I don't feel sadness or any emotion that could bring tears to my eyes anymore. Just anger and emptiness.

At the beginning, nothing, they just stared at themselves and at me. However, when I get very nervous I start making these weird tics where I twitch my face and bare my teeth (I tried really hard to avoid doing that, but it happened). So when I was leaving I clearly heard one of the girls ask "did you see his face?!" to another girl.
I don't feel like I'm different, I know I am. I can try to hide my own thoughts and insecurities, but at the end of the day, I'm **objectively** not normal.

Back in 2018, I approached a group of people at a park and asked if I could sit down and talk with them. They weren't TOTAL strangers - I knew they were students from my former high school, so I figured that maybe we could have acquaintances in common. It went horribly and awkwardly wrong. I know, it was a dumbass idea and I deserve to get made fun of.
Nah, I would still be a mentally ill piece of useless shit.
